item.summary: fix(scripts): build heap ignores its systemd memory budget and takes the full default (#123979) * fix(scripts): size the tsdown heap from the build's own cgroup budget The build heap probe only read the cgroup root (/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max and the v1 equivalent). Those files exist only when the process runs in a namespaced container cgroup; under systemd the budget lives on the process's own slice, and the v2 root carries no limit at all. So every systemd-managed build found no limit, fell back to /proc/meminfo MemTotal, and took the full 12288 MB default heap regardless of its actual budget. Observed on a 15.4 GiB host: openclaw-main-update.service ran tsdown with NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=12288 while its user@999.service slice was bounded at 5 GiB, reaching 3.2 GB RSS and 6.25 GB peak before the host began OOM-killing unrelated services. Resolve the limit from /proc/self/cgroup and walk that chain instead, reading memory.high alongside memory.max (memory.high throttles reclaim rather than failing allocation, so a heap above it stalls the build instead of OOM-ing), and take the tightest bound found.
